title: Sac Brood Virus on Honey bee

Header: Sac Brood Virus on Honey bee
Sac brood virus zero type Sinahala: Mee masi madi virasaya; Tamil: Theny virus

Prevention: Locate bee colonies in a dry and shade area with good ventilation
Clean the bottom board and other parts of the box regularly
Feed the colony adequately in periods with short supply of food
Keep a healthy and egg laying queen
Better to introduce a new queen annually
Replace the older combs with new combs if possible
If colony division is required , select only the healthy colonies
Inspect the colonies at two weeks interval to find any pest damage or diseases
If the colonies are diseased, separate from the healthy ones
Clean hands thoroughly before handling healthy colonies
Clean the tools thoroughly with antiseptics after handling diseased colonies and do not share the tools with healthy colonies
Monitoring: Uncurled diseased larva points outward the head
Diseased larva become yellowish brown and dry
Dead larva appears like a sac filled with liquid when taken out
Dead larvae are removed away from the cells by worker bees
Small holes can be seen on the cell caps in an irregular pattern
No bad smell coming from dead larvae
Worker bees become less active, gather on the bottom board and stay inactive
Several number of eggs (laid by worker bees) can be seen in cells
Direct Control: Control swarming by regular feeding and using the gate
If possible, restrict egg laying by quarantining the queen

At early stage of the disease (less than 5% spread), combine with another colony and feed adequately to maintain a strong colony  At moderate level of infestation (less than 20%) - remove the old queen, introduce a new queen, feed and leave for natural recovery  At serious infestation (more than 20%) - destroy the colony
Restrictions: No chemicals should be used in beehive.
